messages.subject: Documentation or references for next item selection algorithm used in mirtCAT
parts:
Hello Phil,

Can you please suggest me some references where I can read about theory for following methods:


"Drule", "Trule", "Wrule" and "EPrule" etc.


Thanking you,

Irshad

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Documentation or references for next item selection algorithm used in mirtCAT
parts:
The best reference I'm aware of that describes all of these statistics is in a paper currently under review in JSS, which I submitted a while back (and will be shipped with mirtCAT upon publication acceptance). Otherwise, you'll have to refer to the original authors:

Segall DO (1996). “Multidimensional adaptive testing.” Psychometrika, 61, 331–354.

Mulder J, van der Linden WJ (2009). “Multidimensional adaptive testing with optimal design
criteria for item selection.” Psychometrika, 74(2), 273–296.

van der Linden WJ (1999). “Multidimensional adaptive testing with a minimum error-variance
criterion.” Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics, 24, 398–412.

Phil

Many thanks for the mail, Phil.

In "Mulder J, van der Linden WJ (2009). “Multidimensional adaptive testing with optimal design criteria for item selection.” Psychometrika, 74(2), 273–296" reference I found following methods:

D-optimality which maximizes the determinant of information matrix ; mirtCAT manual name- "Drule"

E-optimality maximizes minimum value of the information matrix; mirtCAT manual name- "Erule"

I am confused about 'Trule' ; because in the manual it says , criterion for the maximum (potentially weighted) trace of the information matrix; is this "Trule" same as that of the A-optimality? The doubt is arising because it says that A-optimality criterion chooses that item  that minimizes the trace of the inverse of the information matrix. As far as I know i, in general maximizing trace of a matrix and minimizing trace of its inverse may not fetch you same results.

Also, regarding inclusion of the posterior weight to  'DPrule', 'TPrule', 'EPrule', 'WPrule' ; are they going to be the new methods coined by you? I am asking because I did not find any mention in the references you mentioned in our previous conversation.

Also can you please mention any references where  I can read about 'Wrule' and Kullback-Leibler Information method; these methods I did not find in any of the references you mentioned.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Documentation or references for next item selection algorithm used in mirtCAT
parts:
On Wed, Oct 22, 2014 at 9:24 AM, Irshad Mujawar <irshadmuj...@gmail.com> wrote:
Many thanks for the mail, Phil.

In "Mulder J, van der Linden WJ (2009). “Multidimensional adaptive testing with optimal design criteria for item selection.” Psychometrika, 74(2), 273–296" reference I found following methods:

D-optimality which maximizes the determinant of information matrix ; mirtCAT manual name- "Drule"

E-optimality maximizes minimum value of the information matrix; mirtCAT manual name- "Erule"

I am confused about 'Trule' ; because in the manual it says , criterion for the maximum (potentially weighted) trace of the information matrix; is this "Trule" same as that of the A-optimality? The doubt is arising because it says that A-optimality criterion chooses that item  that minimizes the trace of the inverse of the information matrix. As far as I know i, in general maximizing trace of a matrix and minimizing trace of its inverse may not fetch you same results.

They aren't quite equivalent, but should be very similar. Since the relationship Σ(θ) = inv(FI(θ)) maximizing the (weighted) trace of the information should give very similar results to minimizing the trace of the acov matrix. I opted for the first route since matrix inversion is dangerous business, and can fail in the computations (especially early on) where as working with the information matrix directly doesn't require inversion.

Also, regarding inclusion of the posterior weight to  'DPrule', 'TPrule', 'EPrule', 'WPrule' ; are they going to be the new methods coined by you? I am asking because I did not find any mention in the references you mentioned in our previous conversation.
No they aren't coined, Segall talks about Bayesian variants of the Drule. These are just the analogues for the other methods which include a multivariate prior.
Also can you please mention any references where  I can read about 'Wrule' and Kullback-Leibler Information method; these methods I did not find in any of the references you mentioned.

I think I'm the only one who calls it that. It's just a weighted version where criteria = w^' FI(θ) w, in which case you maximize again. It's similar to the weighted trace function, but also includes covariance information.

Phil
